title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: What has AI-drafted complaining changed about the relationship between drafting quality and the complainant? `[V]`
options: Nothing — well-drafted complaints have always come from well-advised employees
The correlation between an articulate document and an articulate, advised, or well-resourced complainant has been severed
Drafting quality now correlates with the seriousness of the underlying conduct
Complaints are better drafted but shorter
questions.explanation: Which matters because a great deal of informal HR triage ran on exactly that correlation without anyone admitting it. And length went the other way: two pages to eight or twelve.

questions.prompt: Why do minor incidents arrive in protected-characteristic language? `[V]`
options: Because complainants are increasingly aware of their statutory rights
Because a model asked to make a complaint sound serious reaches for the vocabulary the situation seems to call for, and the available vocabulary is bullying, harassment, discrimination, victimisation
Because AI tools are trained on tribunal decisions
Because employees are advised to use statutory language to compel investigation
questions.explanation: Not dishonesty, register. And the consequence is that **the escalated framing is now on the record**: once the document alleges discrimination your response must address discrimination, even where the facts describe something else.

questions.prompt: What is the exposure from downgrading a complaint because it appears AI-drafted? `[V]`
options: A data-protection complaint about automated decision-making
Breach of the Acas Code and potentially victimisation under the Equality Act in the UK; retaliation exposure and loss of the prompt-and-appropriate-response posture in the US
None, provided the decision is documented
A grievance about the grievance procedure
questions.explanation: The rule is the same in both jurisdictions; the citation is not, and the module names the UK authority because that is where direct guidance exists. Specifics to your own counsel.

questions.prompt: Why is treating an AI-drafted submission with extra scepticism described as the same error as extra deference?
options: Because both slow the process down
Because both substitute a judgment about provenance for a judgment about content — and both leave a discoverable trace
Because scepticism and deference are equally difficult to evidence
Because deference is prohibited by the Acas Code
questions.explanation: Which produces the practical discipline: do not record or discuss your view that a submission was AI-drafted. Not because the observation is wrong, but because it is irrelevant to every decision you are about to make.

questions.prompt: What is the crucial asymmetry between allegations and argument?
options: Argument is longer than allegation in most submissions
Only the allegations generate an investigative obligation; the argument must be addressed in your response but does not become an investigation line
Allegations must be investigated within statutory time limits and argument need not be
Argument can be answered by AI and allegations cannot
questions.explanation: Conflating them is what turns a twelve-page document into a twelve-page investigation, and it is why volume feels overwhelming when what changed is the ratio.

questions.prompt: Which step does the module call the highest-value one, and why?
options: Extracting the allegations with a model, because it saves the most time
Having a second person confirm the list, because it catches missed allegations

Sending the numbered list back to the complainant — it corrects your extraction before you build on it, evidences engagement with the whole submission, and prevents the argument that you investigated a narrower version
Recording the time allocated to each allegation
questions.explanation: Ten minutes, and it forecloses Module 4's defect about restating an allegation more narrowly and resolving the narrower version.

questions.prompt: How does the volume trap run in this function?
options: Cheaper production means your function generates more artifacts than it used to
Production got cheaper for the other side, and your obligation per matter did not change
AI-drafted complaints are more likely to be withdrawn, wasting investigative effort
Longer submissions require proportionally longer responses
questions.explanation: Same mechanism as elsewhere in the curriculum, opposite direction. The answer is not reading faster. It is not paying investigative attention to argument.

questions.prompt: Why is labor arbitration described as a forum with no detection apparatus? `[V]`
options: Because arbitrators are not required to give reasons
Because arbitration records are confidential and cannot be checked
Because most arbitrators have no law clerks, no case-law database, and limited power to sanction — so fabricated citations appear and are largely neither reported nor sanctioned
Because arbitration does not rely on precedent
questions.explanation: Which matters precisely because past awards and past practice do real work in contract interpretation: a fabricated authority can enter the precedent conversation and stay. Verify your own citations and check theirs.
